# AGENTS.md

<!-- agent-rules v1.0.0 · generated by `agent-rules sync` · do NOT edit above the divider: change shared rules in the agent-rules repo, and this project's guide in AGENTS.project.md -->

Single source of truth for AI agents working in this repository. The other entry
files — `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` — only point here, so whichever agent a
contributor uses (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Zed, …) reads the same
guide.

Two halves: **Working rules** (how to work here — traps to avoid) and, below the
divider, a **Project guide** (what this project is and how it is built).

## Keeping the rules useful

- The Working rules are **traps to avoid, not a map to follow**. Add a rule only
  if it is (1) **non-obvious**, (2) **hit more than once**, and (3) **specific
  enough to act on**. Prefer fixing an existing rule to adding a vague one.
- These rules are shared across projects — don't edit them inline here. Change
  them in the `agent-rules` repo and re-run `agent-rules sync`.
- The Project guide below is the map. Keep it current, but don't let it sprawl —
  deep detail belongs in `docs/` and the code.

## Working discipline

- **Do what was asked — no more.** Avoid unrequested "creative additions" and
  scope creep. If you spot adjacent work worth doing, mention it; don't silently
  do it.
- **Match the surrounding code** — its naming, comment density, and idioms. New
  code should read like the file it lives in.
- **Prefer editing existing files** to creating many small new ones. Add a new
  file only for a genuinely new logical component.
- **Report faithfully.** If tests fail, say so with the output; if you skipped a
  step, say so. Don't claim something works until you've verified it.

## Comments

- Comments explain **why**, not **what**. Don't restate the code or narrate its
  structure. Write a comment only for a non-obvious reason a reader would
  otherwise miss.

## Names

- Use **full words**. No cryptic abbreviations (`queue`, not `q`) — except a
  framework's own established convention already used by the surrounding code.

## Error handling

- **Never silently discard errors.** Don't drop a fallible result with
  `let _ = ...`. Handle it: propagate it, log it with intent, or branch on it.
- **Surface failures to where they matter.** An operation that affects the UI
  should let its error reach the UI, so the user gets real feedback instead of a
  silent no-op.

## Language

Everything committed to this repository is in **English** — source code,
identifiers, user-facing strings, comments, commit messages, PR descriptions, and
docs — even when the working conversation is in another language. Project-specific
exceptions (localization catalogs, deliberately non-English generated output) are
noted in the Project guide below.

## Commits

- Commit only when the user asks.
- Split large or multi-stage work into several focused commits, one logical change
  each, rather than one sweeping commit.
- Keep unrelated pre-existing changes out of your commits — stage explicit paths,
  not `git add -A`.
- Use conventional-commit prefixes (`feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`,
  `test`), with an optional scope, e.g. `feat(core): …`. Imperative mood.
- Do not add AI tools as commit authors or co-authors — no `Co-Authored-By` trailer
  and no "Generated with" line. Commits carry only the human author. The project's
  one AI acknowledgment lives in the README.

## Pull requests

- **Title:** conventional-commit prefix matching this repo's commit conventions —
  e.g. `feat(core): add music lens`. Imperative mood, no trailing punctuation.
- **Body:** say *what* changed and *why*, and flag anything reviewers should look
  at closely.
- Don't put AI attribution in the PR — the project's one acknowledgment lives in
  the README.

---

## What this is

`agent-rules` is the shared AI-agent guidance for our projects: the `rules/*.md`
modules plus a zero-dependency Node CLI (`bin/agent-rules`) that vendors them into
each project's `AGENTS.md`. This repo **dogfoods its own guidance** — the
`AGENTS.md` you are reading was generated by the CLI from this repo's own rules
(`source: "."`). See the README for the full model, the new-project checklist,
and the release flow.

## Layout

- `rules/` — the shared rule modules (`_intro`, `core`, `language`, `commits`,
  `pull-requests`, and per-stack `rust` / `typescript-react` / `godot`).
- `bin/agent-rules` — the sync CLI (Node, zero dependencies).
- `templates/` — starters copied into a project: `.agentrules.json`,
  `AGENTS.project.md`, and the drift-check workflow `agent-rules.yml`.
- `consumers.json` — repos the release fan-out targets. This repo is deliberately
  **not** listed: it is the source, not a downstream consumer.
- `VERSION` — the version the CLI stamps into every generated `AGENTS.md`.
- `.github/workflows/` — `release.yml` (tag → dispatch fan-out) and
  `self-check.yml` (verify this repo's own `AGENTS.md` is in sync).

## Working on the rules

- Edit `rules/*.md`, then re-run `node bin/agent-rules sync` so this repo's own
  `AGENTS.md` stays current (the `self-check` workflow enforces it).
- Rules are **traps to avoid** — keep them non-obvious, specific, and repeatedly
  hit; the meta-rules at the top of any generated `AGENTS.md` apply here too.
- Cut a release by bumping `VERSION` and tagging `vX.Y.Z` (README → *Cutting a
  release*); that fans out a bump PR to every consumer.

## Build & test

No build step — the CLI is plain Node:

```bash
node bin/agent-rules sync            # regenerate this repo's AGENTS.md
node bin/agent-rules sync --check    # verify it is in sync (used by self-check CI)
```
